definitions.explanation: A small police station found on street corners in Japan.

examples.japanese: {交番|こうばん}で{道|みち}を{聞|き}きました。
examples.english: I asked for directions at the police box.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}に{交番|こうばん}があります。
examples.english: There is a police box in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {財布|さいふ}を{交番|こうばん}に{届|とど}けた。
examples.english: I turned in the wallet at the police box.

examples.japanese: {落|お}とし{物|もの}を{交番|こうばん}に{届|とど}けた。
examples.english: I took the lost item to the police box.

examples.japanese: {近所|きんじょ}の{交番|こうばん}のおまわりさんはとても{親切|しんせつ}だ。
examples.english: The officer at the neighborhood police box is very kind.

notes:
A small neighborhood police station found on street corners throughout Japan. Staffed by one or two officers, these are a uniquely Japanese institution recognized internationally.

COMMON FUNCTIONS:
- Giving directions to lost pedestrians
- Receiving {落|お}とし{物|もの} (lost items)
- Handling minor incidents and disputes
- Community patrol and crime prevention

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {交番|こうばん}で{道|みち}を{聞|き}く: to ask for directions at a police box
- {交番|こうばん}に{届|とど}ける: to turn something in at a police box

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {交番|こうばん} system is a model of community policing that has been adopted by other countries. Officers are expected to know the local neighborhood well and maintain friendly relations with residents.

RELATED TERMS:
- {警察署|けいさつしょ}: police station (larger, full-service)
- {警官|けいかん}: police officer (neutral)
- おまわりさん: policeman (friendly/informal term, used by children)
